title: Best Product of Two Digits
statement:
You get an integer n with at least two digits. Choose two digits of n at different positions and multiply them.

Return the largest product you can get. A digit value may be used twice only if it appears at least twice in n.

examples.why: The two largest digits are 9 and 4.
9 appears once, so 9 × 9 is not allowed. The best is 9 × 7.
The two 5s are at different positions, so 5 × 5 is allowed.

hints: Digits are never negative. Which two digits can give the biggest product?
The product of non-negative numbers is largest when both factors are as large as possible: take the two largest digits.
Track the largest and second largest digit in one pass, treating a repeated digit as two separate entries.

explain.intuition:
All digits are between 0 and 9, so there are no negative numbers to flip a product's sign. Making either factor bigger never makes the product smaller, so the answer is the product of the two largest digits, counted by position.

"Counted by position" is the part people miss. In 1907 the biggest digit is 9, but there is only one 9, so the best is 9 × 7. In 5050 there are two 5s, and 5 × 5 is fine. Keeping a top-two pair, like tracking the two highest scores in a leaderboard, handles both cases.
steps: If d ≥ first, set second = first and first = d. Otherwise if d > second, set second = d.
pitfalls: Squaring the largest digit. That is only allowed if the digit appears twice.
Using a set of distinct digits, which loses the second copy of a repeated digit, as in 5050 or 7777.
Using d > first instead of d ≥ first in the top-two update, so a second equal maximum never reaches second.

solutions.title: Try every pair of positions
solutions.idea: Turn n into its digit list and multiply every pair of different positions.

solutions.title: Keep the top two digits
solutions.idea: One pass over the digits tracks the largest and second-largest, counting repeats separately.

followups: Return the largest product of k digits at different positions.
n is now an array of signed integers. Why are the two largest values no longer enough?
